title: Raising the Destination Loading Line on a Travel Protection Plans Certificate
content:
A Travel Protection Plans certificate declares a destination region, and the destination loading that region attracts is charged to the policyholder as a premium line in its own right. This page states what that charge governs and how the desk records it.

## When the charge arises

The charge arises on a certificate whose declared region attracts a destination loading and whose premium record does not yet carry that loading. What is governed is the amount of the destination loading line and the raising of that line against the certificate. The line is charged on the certificate as a whole rather than on any one insured traveller, and it stands as a routine issue charge on the policyholder's premium statement.

## How the line is raised

The desk records the charge with the travel protection desk tool `charge_destination_loading_6e26c317`, which is not listed among the ordinary tools: the representative unlocks it and then calls it. One call posts a single premium line of the destination loading kind against the named certificate, charged to the named policyholder, for the amount given and through the channel given, dated the day it is posted.

## What each parameter carries

| Parameter | What it is | Form |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `care_policy_id` | The reference number of the travel protection policy record the loading is charged to | Read from the policy record returned by the policy finder |
| `customer_id` | The reference number of the traveller profile the premium is charged to | Read from the traveller profile returned by the profile finder |
| `amount_usd` | The amount of the loading line | A USD amount with 2 decimal places, always positive, rounded half to even at the cent; held in US dollars whatever currency it is presented in, never left empty |
| `payment_channel` | The channel the premium line is taken through | Exactly one of the four channels below, and never anything else |

The four channels the `payment_channel` parameter accepts are `web`, where the policyholder settles the line themselves on the website; `mobile_app`, where the policyholder settles the line themselves in the mobile application; `call_centre`, where the line is taken by a desk representative during a telephone call; and `corporate_portal`, where the line is billed through the corporate travel programme portal rather than to the traveller directly.

## What the call returns

The call returns a single confirmation sentence. It names the reference number of the premium line created, which is a text reference beginning cpe_, the reference number of the certificate it was posted to, and the amount posted in US dollars to two decimal places. The presence of the new line reference in that sentence is what indicates the line was posted; there is no other success flag.
